host.timer: cntvct_el0 at 1.05 GHz; PMCCNTR_EL0 SIGILLs from userspace on the virtualized instance, so the coarse virtual counter averaged over a dependency chain was used and was sufficient

regenerable: only on an aarch64 host. This is an acquired observation, like the pair's ARM key recovery and the imported nonce-leak traces, not a number bin/regen.py produces on the x86 build host. The acquisition script is pairs/kyberslash/graviton/.

codegen.note: the KyberSlash vulnerable source emits a hardware division only at -Os, the same pattern as x86 (idiv only at -Os), now on a third architecture

udiv_latency_operand_dependent.note: serial dependency chain; ticks/udiv rises with dividend magnitude, matching ARM's documented W-form 5 to 12 cycle range

kyberslash_operand_range_step.note: a step at dividend = divisor = 3329: below it the quotient is 0 and udiv finishes one iteration sooner. The leak is one bit per coefficient, whether the coefficient exceeds about 833.

end_to_end_coeff_to_bit_Os.note: real KyberSlash reduction, two-class fixed-vs-random over low and high coefficients

conclusion: The KyberSlash leak class reproduces on Graviton3 as a ~1-cycle, one-bit-per-coefficient leak (a step at dividend = divisor), much quieter than the tens-of-cycles software-division leak on Cortex-A7 (ARMv7, no hardware divider, __aeabi_idiv). A virtualized c7g suffices to measure it. This extends the corpus's (vendor x optimisation-level) toolchain finding to (x microarchitecture): the same source, the same -Os build, leaks at tens of cycles on Cortex-A7 and about one cycle on Neoverse V1.
tier_note: This is a leak-PRESENCE measurement, not a key recovery. No recovery was run on Graviton, so the KyberSlash pair stays tier C. A recovery adapted to one-bit-per-coefficient information would make it tier A, and this measurement shows that is feasible on rented hardware for roughly one dollar.
